content.text: I reviewed the complete package as provided — brief, conversation, disclosure, all ten draft sections, the numeral ledger, and all five figure briefs — and built a full source ledger before returning.

input.summary:
Full source-fidelity preflight completed against input/disclosure.md as the sole technical authority (the conversation's single USER passage is a truncated duplicate of that disclosure and adds nothing; input/brief.md was used only for title, applicant/inventor, no-priority and no-government-support formalities; input/request.md is a repair instruction and was not treated as affirmative disclosure).

Ledger traced, item by item: every limitation of claims 1-10 (apparatus), 11-13 (installed clamp assembly), and 14-17 (method) maps to an exact affirmative disclosure sentence — semicircular halves plus hinge and releasable latch; three jaw carriages in radial guides; pivoting concave jaw pads that seat "without requiring a tool-specific pipe diameter"; outward-biasing carriage springs; segmented cam ring retained in an annular guide with one segment carried by each half; complementary drive faces at the hinge and latch ends that couple the segments on closure; followers in respective oblique slots; wedge on the latch bearing a drive face of the ring and rotating it through a limited stroke; synchronized equal inward travel; the two latch positions including the over-center position; the force-limiting spring stack between latch handle and wedge absorbing post-contact travel; the visible indicator pin moving relative to a fixed edge of the latch housing at a predetermined compression range and expressly not measuring pipe diameter; the optional mounting boss outside the annular guide for a sensor, tool or conduit that does not participate in jaw synchronization; and both the installation and removal sequences. No dependent-claim limitation and no optional embodiment lacks an affirmative passage. The drafting agent's own prose in conversation.md refers to a "self-adhering layer with a microsuction surface"; that feature appears nowhere in the reviewed text, so no unsupported matter was carried in from it.

Numerals: all 28 entries (10-66, with 28 unused) were checked. Each designates exactly one part in the description, the ledger, and every figure brief; the two distinct drive-face families are properly disambiguated (44/46/48/50 segment-coupling faces versus 54 ring drive face acted on by the wedge), and no numeral is reused or undefined. Every numeral mentioned in the description appears on at least one sheet, and every numeral listed in a figure's front matter has a matching placement target and "Numerals shown" entry (FIG. 1: 8; FIG. 2: 5; FIG. 3: 8; FIG. 4: 7; FIG. 5: 5).

Figure briefs: geometry statements were tested against the functional-surface rule. The oblique-slot inclination and the shared rotational sense of the three slots are entailed by "oblique slots translate that rotation into synchronized inward travel of all three jaw carriages"; the abutting, matching-outline segment end faces are entailed by "complementary drive faces ... couple the segments"; pad-only pipe contact is entailed by "carries a pivoting concave jaw pad that bears on a pipe"; the handle-stack-wedge series in FIG. 4 is entailed by "a force-limiting spring stack lies between the latch handle and the wedge"; and the pin projecting past the housing top wall is the minimal realization of the disclosed visible pin read against a fixed edge. No brief verbalizes an undisclosed taper, ramp angle, seat depth, runout direction, or end-position of a functional face; end-face shape, wedge, housing, boss, hinge, latch body and pad outlines are expressly schematic and remain generic. Orientation is consistent across sheets (hinge at the left break, latch at the right break, first half/first segment upper, second half/second segment lower, so 44/46 at the left junction and 48/50 at the right junction agree with the description's assignments).

Text consistency: claims and description use identical relationships and terms (ring drive face, coupled cam ring, limited stroke, over-center position, drive path, tool specific pipe diameter); claim antecedents are supported; no means-plus-function language appears; the Brief Description of the Drawings matches the five briefs; there are no section lines to reconcile; the Field, Summary, Detailed Description and Abstract contain no "by way of example," "any closed outline," or other statement added to justify a renderer's visual choice, so the depiction conventions stay confined to the figure files; and no drafting note, placeholder, open question, instruction, unresolved alternative, or internal comment remains anywhere in the draft. Cross-reference and government-support sections read "Not applicable," matching the brief's no-priority, no-federal-funding instructions, and the title matches the brief verbatim. Background prior-art characterizations were not assessed for inventor support, per scope. No unsupported technical assertion and no internal inconsistency was found.

Representative traces: "three jaw carriages ... slidable in a respective radial guide ... jaw pad ... mounted for pivoting movement ... concave bearing surface" to "Three radial jaw carriages are distributed around the closed frame. Each carriage slides in a radial guide and carries a pivoting concave jaw pad that bears on a pipe without requiring a tool-specific pipe diameter"; the segmented ring, per-half carriage of segments, and the four complementary drive faces 44/46/48/50 to "A segmented cam ring is retained in an annular guide of the frame. One cam-ring segment is carried by each frame half. When the halves close, complementary drive faces at the hinge and latch ends couple the segments so that they move as one ring"; follower 40, oblique slot 38, wedge 52, ring drive face 54 and limited stroke to "Each jaw carriage has a follower received in a respective oblique slot of the cam ring. Closing the latch drives a wedge against a drive face of the cam ring and rotates the coupled ring through a limited stroke. The oblique slots translate that rotation into synchronized inward travel of all three jaw carriages"; carriage spring 42 and the retraction sequence to "A spring biases each carriage outward when the latch is released" and "the carriage springs retract the jaws before the frame halves are opened"; the two latch positions, spring stack 62 in the handle-to-wedge drive path, indicator pin 64 and fixed edge 60 to the third disclosure paragraph verbatim in substance, including "does not measure pipe diameter"; mounting boss 66 and claims 8/13/17 to "The frame may carry a mounting boss outside the annular guide for supporting a sensor, tool, or conduit. The mounting boss does not participate in jaw synchronization"; the assembly claim's pipe element and the method steps of claims 14–17 to the installation and removal paragraphs.

Figure briefs were checked against the functional-surface-geometry standard. The junction end faces in FIG-3 are stated only as "two short faces of matching outline that abut one another" with "The shape of these end faces is shown schematically", and no taper, angle, depth, runout, circumferential end position, or contact topology beyond the disclosed complementary engagement is verbalized; the ring drive face is kept as "a short plain drive face on the band" with no undisclosed end position; the slot inclination statements go no further than the disclosed conversion of common rotation into synchronized inward travel of all three carriages; the housing, wedge, spring column, rod and handle in FIG-4 assert only the disclosed drive-path order (handle, spring stack, wedge) and the disclosed pin-relative-to-fixed-edge reading. No figure brief's depiction convention leaks into the application text: the description and Brief Description contain no "by way of example" shape hedge, no "any closed outline" language, and no optional embodiment added to justify a rendered outline.

Internal consistency verified: claims and description use identical relationships and terms (hinge end / latch end, coupled cam ring, limited stroke, ring drive face, over-center position, force-limiting spring stack, carriage spring); each numeral has exactly one referent across ledger, description and figures; the upper/lower half-to-segment assignments (12/32 upper, 14/34 lower) and the hinge-left/latch-right convention are consistent across FIG-1, FIG-2, FIG-3 and FIG-4; every ledger numeral appears on at least one sheet and every sheet numeral is described in the text; the five entries in the Brief Description of the Drawings match the five figure briefs in view type and content; there are no named section lines requiring matched designations; and no drafting note, placeholder, open question, unresolved alternative or internal comment remains in any application section. The stale drafting-agent message in input/conversation.md referring to a "self-adhering layer with a microsuction surface" is labeled YOU, is not inventor support, and no such feature appears anywhere in the draft, so no unsupported matter entered from it. Background prior-art characterizations were not traced to the disclosure, as instructed; their sourcing is left to the later citation review.
